- When sentiment is consistently negative or mixed in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 3–5% relative to prior peak.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 10–15% below peak for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment shows strong bullish momentum (e.g., 3+ consecutive +1.00), model tends to overreact; apply downward bias of 2–4% for next 5–7 days.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >10% above 30-day moving average, reduce by 1–3% per day until convergence.
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish (e.g., +1 → -1), model often lags; adjust forecast 2–3 days ahead to reflect sentiment reversal.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome is consistently below 60% of 30-day high, model is overconfident; apply 5–10% downward correction across entire horizon.
